elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Revised Article XXIV(c): "except that Licensee may assign without consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets"; "AFFILIATE" is a defined term (Section 1.1), so the carve-out is anchored.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same inserted exception expressly names "a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets" and dispenses with consent. The retained routing sentence sends any Change of Control to Article XX, which as revised imposes no consent or termination consequence, so the carve-out is not neutralised.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "Licensor may not assign this Agreement without Licensee's prior written consent" — a direct reciprocal restriction that did not exist in the original.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Same added sentence: "which shall not be unreasonably withheld."

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Same added sentence: "and may not assign to a competitor of Licensee" — an unqualified bar, not merely a reasonableness factor.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Article XX(a) rewritten: "A Change of Control ... shall not terminate this Agreement or any of Licensee's rights or licenses hereunder and shall give Licensor no right to terminate this Agreement." The automatic-termination trigger and the deemed-reasonable-refusal proviso are gone, while the "CHANGE OF CONTROL" definition survives so the sentence has a defined trigger.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: Only Licensee gets a consent-free successor route; the added Licensor sentence bars any Licensor assignment (including to a successor) absent Licensee's prior written consent, so the mutual successor right is absent.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: No notice mechanic appears anywhere in the rendered language; the Licensee carve-out is silent on notifying Licensor.

The retained/inserted text creates a no-consent non-successor exception (assignment to an Affiliate), which under the ASSIGN fallback boundary defeats a clean "other assignments require consent" result.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Licensee-side consent in Article XXIV(c) remains unqualified ("without Licensor's prior written consent", no reasonableness standard); only the new Licensor-side sentence carries the standard.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: all six atomic elements are carried in operative language (consent-free Affiliate/successor carve-out for Licensee, Licensor assignment subject to Licensee's non-unreasonably-withheld consent, absolute bar on assignment to a Licensee competitor, and express removal of any Change of Control termination right).

Fallback level is incomplete (no written-notice mechanic, no mutual successor right, Affiliate no-consent exception, and no reasonableness standard on Licensee-side consent), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully met.

Minimality holds: the change-of-control edit removes only the automatic-termination trigger and its now-orphaned consent proviso/deemed-reasonable gloss (all of which exist solely to operate the termination right), retains the "CHANGE OF CONTROL" definition, retains Article XX(b), and retains verbatim the Customer-favourable routing sentence and the successors-and-permitted-assigns tail. The Licensee carve-out is drafted as a narrow "except that" exception rather than a rewrite, and no notwithstanding override, survival tail, or extraneous procedure is added.

Intent is preserved: no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created (the Section 13.4(a) reference is pre-existing and untouched), and the Article XXII right of first refusal on a sale/merger survives without contradiction — a process right is not inconsistent with a consent-free successor assignment, and it is properly left to the ROFR/MFN rule.

Drafting note (not a defect): the retained sentence "Any attempt to assign ... without such consent will be void" now reads against a clause where affiliate/successor transfers require no consent, so it cannot bite; if the counterparty pushes back, consider appending ", other than an assignment permitted by the foregoing exception" for clarity.

Severity remains high: the original clause was walk-away (blanket Licensee assignment bar plus automatic termination on Customer change of control with deemed-reasonable refusal), and the redline is the minimum needed to clear it.
